cefrAlignment: Matches B1 overall listening comprehension (following the main points and key details of clear standard speech on familiar everyday matters): the clips are 105–136 words of slow, clear service dialogues, the vocabulary is high-frequency, and the tasks are gist, detail and one-step self-corrections.
examFidelity: IELTS Part 1-style note completion with a ONE OR TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER limit and in-order answers, plus TOEIC Part 3-style gist, detail and next-action MCQs, are accurate to exams.ts; the IELTS tip wrongly said Part 1 starts with an example, which IELTS removed in 2020, and it is now corrected.
fixes: IELTS tip in Learn: removed the outdated claim that Part 1 starts with an example (IELTS dropped it in 2020); it now says there is no example and the recording is heard once, as exams.ts states
ex2 gap 1 (time): added the accepted answers 'half five', '5.30 p.m.' and '5:30 p.m.'
ex2 gap 4: added 'my umbrella' as an accepted answer
ex4 dictation sentence 1: removed the number 'four', because learners who typed '4' were marked wrong by the word-by-word checker
openConcerns: The answer key accepts 'half past five' (three words) under a ONE OR TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER limit, on the basis that it is the number written in words. A specialist may prefer a stricter key.
Browser TTS gives each speaker a different voice, but the prosody of corrections such as 'No, wait …' was not checked by ear.
learnerOutcome: A learner who does this lesson well can work out who, where and why in a short service conversation, write down key details, and ignore information that the speaker later corrects.
